walk.summary: Row O passes again on the fixed build (0deff9c4) for everything a sandbox reaches. The run used encrypted, locked-at-boot seeded and empty folders, unlocked through the real form, in en/fr/ar/zh and at 375 px, with 0 page errors and nothing going online. Pass: O1-O10, O12, and the encrypted-throwaway analogs O13a, O14a and O15a. Not measurable here: the online half of O11 and O13-O15 on the maintainer's real install. All four confirmed row-O defects are fixed. O2: the coach covers no control in any locale or width and re-anchors in RTL. O1: the backup-row reason is translated ×3. O4: the task-manager tab title is translated and follows live switches. O3 still reads '(0 files · 0 B)' for an absent lane, which was judged by design. Five new P3s, none blocking: (1) the coach now sits over the first lines of the tab content and hides part of the Living sources caveat until 'Not now'; (2) the scheduler targets line is English in fr/ar, with no defect id or deferral tracking it; (3) a live language switch collapses open diffs on Living sources; (4) fr translates 'lane' as both 'file' and 'voie'; (5) zh composed lines insert an ASCII space after full-width punctuation. items.ref: new:The offline coach now sits over the first lines of the tab content, hiding part of the Living sources caveat until 'Not now'
items.evidence:
I used my own fresh encrypted instance A: dataA seeded from the tree with the row's two seeds (living-sources then storage-budgets, byte-identical to the repo copies), OO_DB_PASSPHRASE set and OO_DB_PLAINTEXT unset. The first bytes of both open_omniscience.db and wiki.db are ciphertext. It booted on 8968 with /api/system/lock-state = locked and was unlocked through #pw/#btn-unlock. Each case ran in a fresh Chromium context, so the coach was on its first or second launch. Figures are from /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/O-recheck/raw-r1.json.

How much of #living-caveat was under the coach:
- en 1440: 92 of 372 sampled points (coach [984,125,1254,297], z-index 52). The h2 had 69 of 279 under it.
- fr 1440: 92 of 372. zh 1440: 46 of 186.
- ar 1440: 88 of 372, at the caveat's left end (coach [186,125,456,260]).
- en 375: 100 of 325, and 140 of 175 for the h2.
- Settings → Data & backup → Storage, en: #storage-reading had 115 of 465 under it, which clips the reference-machine line.
- After 'Not now': 0 of 372.

With the page at the top, no control's centre was under the coach (covered: [] every time) and no nav click was intercepted, so the B3 fix holds there.

One case is worse than the walker described. On instance B, I opened Settings → Advanced → Collection → Advanced (legacy) and scrolled to #sched-targets. The fixed coach then covered a control: coach_cover.covered = ['#sch-pages: 50'], the 'Max pages / source' input (raw-r4-B.json coach_scrolled_adv).

The cap on launches is real: app-core.js:1152 stops the coach once seen >= 6.

Shots (in /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/O-recheck/shots/): R1-coach-living-en-1440.png, R1-coach-living-ar-1440.png, R1-coach-living-en-375.png, R1-coach-storage-en-1440.png, R1-living-en-1440-after-notnow.png, R1s-coach-over-adv-scrolled-en.png. R5-maps-zh.png shows the same over the Maps caveat.

In the 375 shot, the 'Pages the live stream follows…' bubble is a harness artifact: the mouse was left over the card after the hamburger nav. It is not part of this finding.
items.root_cause: src/static/app-core.js:1104-1120 (_placeCoach). The fix for O-2 always sets top = guardBottom + gap, where guardBottom is the bottom of .chrome and the protected top-bar buttons. That is exactly where every tab-page begins: its h2 and its visible-by-default .card-caveat (#living-caveat, index.html:1485) sit there. src/static/app.css:1870 makes #net-coach position:fixed, so it also covers whatever the user scrolls under it. The guard (_COACH_GUARD, app-core.js:1101) protects only the chrome and buttons, never caveat text or form controls in the content.
items.suggested_fix: Stop overlaying content. Render the coach in the page flow as a slim strip inside .chrome, under the top bar and with the arrow pointing at the plane, so it pushes the tab content down instead of covering it. The ResizeObserver on .chrome (app-core.js:1168-1171) already re-places things when the chrome's height changes. If it must stay a floating bubble, add the active tab's h2, its visible .card-caveat elements and any focusable control to the guard rects. When no free rectangle exists below the chrome, fall back to a compact placement that covers nothing, for example the bottom corner of .main-col, or collapse the bubble to a dot on the plane.

On instance A at 8968 and on my own instance B at 9068 (empty encrypted corpus plus scheduler_settings.json {mode: markets}, booted locked and unlocked through the form), #sched-targets reads '0 sources targeted of 0 enabled · this run will process up to 0 / by language: — / by type: —' in all three cases below, in en, fr and ar:

- on a fresh load of the panel, before any press;

Everything around it is translated: the button, the retired-mode notice ('Le mode « Marchés »…', 'أُلغي وضع «الأسواق»…'), the summaries and the crawl hint (raw-r2-A.json item2, raw-r2-B.json; shots R2-B-targets-fr.png, R2-B-targets-ar.png, R2-A-legacy-targets-fr.png).

No string in the line has a key in fr.json.

The line is not tracked anywhere as a deferral:
- The gate's O12 calls it a 'Known leftover', but that is an acknowledgement, not a ruling.
- The 2026-09-26 OPEN_QUEUE entry's 'Deferred from the fixes' list does not include it.
- No defect id tracks it.
- docs/audit/scheduler-lanes-clickthrough-2026-09-25/README.md:19 only calls it out of scope.

The gate's wording ('the line the "Preview targets" button prints') is also inaccurate. loadScheduler calls previewTargets() every time the panel opens (app-sources.js:1491), and Save calls it too (:1576).
items.root_cause: src/static/app-sources.js:1520-1523 (previewTargets) builds the line from a hard-coded English template literal ('sources targeted', 'of … enabled · this run will process up to', 'by language:', 'by type:') with no t()/tf(). Write 'by language' and 'by type' through ooLabelHtml so each locale supplies its own separator. Keep the last /api/scheduler/targets payload and re-render it from app-boot.js's oo:langchange listener. Correct the O12 gate text to say the line renders when the panel opens.

items.ref: new:A live language switch collapses an open diff on Living sources (stream 'Show diff' and Law 'Stored diff')
items.evidence:
Clean reproduction (raw-r3-clean.json):
1. Living sources → Wikipedia. Click the 'Walk Tracked Page' button first, then 'Show diff' on the Walk Rome +38 row. The diff is open and the button reads 'Hide diff' (shot R3c-a-before-en.png).
2. Switch to Français through #lang-switch. .living-diff is gone and the button reads 'Afficher le diff' (R3c-a-after-fr.png).
3. The tracked page is kept: #wiki-tc-title still reads 'en · Walk Tracked Page', with 16 rows.
4. Law: open 'Stored diff' (details[open] = true), then switch fr→ar. It is closed (R3c-law-after-ar.png). The same happened fr→zh in raw-r2-A.json item3.

The walker's own evidence did not isolate the switch. In extra.py, 'Walk Tracked Page' is clicked AFTER 'Show diff', and that click alone collapses the diff. The walker's before.diff_btn already reads 'Show diff'. So live_fr.diff_open=false did not prove the switch closed it. My run above does prove it (see also the new tracked-page item below).
items.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:259: the oo:langchange listener calls showLivingView(_livingView). That goes through src/static/app-living.js:275 to loadLivingStream(), which re-fetches and replaces the list (app-living.js:325, box.innerHTML = html), dropping every filled #living-diff-N box. For Law it goes to loadLivingLaw(), which rebuilds the list (app-living.js:382) with closed <details>. Only the tracked page is explicitly restored (app-boot.js:260, loadWikiTC).
items.suggested_fix: Before re-rendering on oo:langchange, record the open stream diffs (revision ids of non-empty #living-diff-* boxes) and the open law <details> (give each one a data-change-id). Then re-render from the cached payload and re-open them: call livingShowDiff(id) for each open revision, and set details.open for each recorded law id. Or re-translate the existing rows in place instead of rebuilding them. Add a Node test that opens a diff, dispatches oo:langchange and asserts the diff is still open.

items.ref: new:fr: 'lane' is translated two ways across row-O surfaces ('file' and 'voie')
items.evidence:
In Français (raw-r2-A.json item4):
- The Storage header reads 'FILE' (CSS upper-cases 'File').
- The Wikipedia lane hover reads 'Le fichier de base de données propre à la file Wikipédia…'.
- The Export / Sauvegarder… hover on 'Sources vivantes' reads 'une voie est une base de données chiffrée vivante ; son format de sauvegarde n'est pas encore arrêté'.
- The Collection summary reads '— planification, voies, ingestion manuelle et par lots'.

On instance B (raw-r2-B.json), the retired notice reads '…s'exécutent désormais comme une voie…'.

The consent popup hint only appears in protected mode with a proxy. Under the default transparent mode the hint names no lane: 'Le mode protégé est désactivé…'. I set protected mode with socks5h://127.0.0.1:9 on my throwaway B, as the walker's O8b did, and put it back afterwards. The fr hint then reads 'Les requêtes transitent par le proxy que vous avez configuré ; une file ne repasse jamais d'elle-même…' (raw-r4-B.json fr_hint; shot R4-consent-protected-fr.png). The popup was cancelled and /api/system/network read {online:false}.

In fr.json, among the 36 keys containing 'lane', 26 use 'file' and 10 use 'voie'. Even the two sibling hints of one function disagree: _transportHint uses 'file' for proxy (fr.json:3392) and 'voie' for pool (fr.json:4535). ar ('المسار') and zh ('通道') are consistent.
items.root_cause:
The two terms in src/static/locales/fr.json:
- 'file': lines 3392, 4478 and 4506 ('Lane': 'File'), and 23 other lane keys.
- 'voie': lines 4374, 4400, 4462, 4469, 4470, 4529, 4535 and 4737.
No French glossary entry or ruling fixes the term, so translation batches chose independently.
items.suggested_fix: Choose one French term and align all 36 lane keys to it. I suggest 'voie': the upper-cased 'FILE' header reads as the English word 'file', and 'la file' sits awkwardly beside 'fichier' in the Storage hover. Then add a small glossary check to scripts/i18n_report.py that flags any fr value for a key containing 'lane' that lacks the chosen term, so a later batch cannot reintroduce the split.

'HTTP 503 from the mirror' itself is the seeded error, shown verbatim by design (the _jobWhy comment says the failure is shown verbatim), so it is not part of this finding.
items.root_cause:
Three places weld an ASCII space after a translated label:
- src/static/app-settings.js:1856: `${esc(lead)} ${esc(bits.join(" · "))}`, where lead is '本机（启动时读取）：'.
- src/static/app-settings.js:1889: `${esc(line)} ${esc(t("That is more than the drive has free."))}`, where line ends in '。'.
- src/static/app-core.js:2099 (_jobWhy): `t("Failed:") + " " + j.error`. The Living sources Maps table (app-living.js:252) and the task manager both use this.
The app already has the right tool, ooLabelHtml/ooLabelText (app-core.js:36-57), which uses the keyed '{prefix}: {text}' frame ('{prefix}：{text}' in zh/ja, '{prefix} : {text}' in fr). These sites do not use it.
items.suggested_fix:
Change three calls:
- app-settings.js:1856: ooLabelHtml(esc(stripColon(lead)), esc(bits.join(' · '))), or re-key lead without its colon.
- app-core.js:2099: ooLabelText(t('Failed'), j.error).
- app-settings.js:1889: join the two sentences with a keyed frame such as tf('{a} {b}') whose zh/ja value is '{a}{b}', or fold them into one tf sentence.
Then sweep the same `t("Failed:") + " "` pattern at app-backup.js:2976, app-diagnostics.js:1155/1228/1294/1553, app-gov-law.js:971/973 and app-settings.js:859/904/915.

recheck.summary:
I reproduced all five of the walker's items on my own fresh encrypted instances and confirm each one as a P3 defect on build 0deff9c4. I also found one related new P3.

**Setup**
- Instance A (dataA, port 8968): the row's two seeds, run from the tree. Instance B (dataB, port 9068): an empty corpus plus scheduler_settings.json {mode: markets}. No existing data folder was copied.
- Both were seeded with OO_DB_PASSPHRASE set and OO_DB_PLAINTEXT unset; the database headers are ciphertext.
- Both booted locked and were unlocked through the #pw/#btn-unlock form.
- Chromium headless with the required flags and no proxy variables. No page errors, console errors or HTTP ≥ 400 in any run.
- Both server logs contain no POST /api/system/network, and /api/system/network read {online:false} at the end. Both servers were stopped by PID, ports 8968 and 9068 are free, and the tree is still clean (git status empty, no .pyc).

**Findings**
1. **Coach over the Living sources caveat.** Confirmed: 92 of 372 caveat points are under the coach in en and fr at 1440, 88 of 372 in ar, and 100 of 325 at 375 px. It also clips the Storage reference-machine line (115 of 465). It is worse than the walker described: once the page is scrolled, the fixed coach covers a control, the 'Max pages / source' input (#sch-pages).
2. **Targets line stays English.** Confirmed in en, fr and ar, both before and after pressing the button. The line renders on every panel open (app-sources.js:1491). No ruling, OPEN_QUEUE entry or defect id tracks it; the gate's O12 only calls it a "known leftover".
3. **A live language switch collapses open diffs.** Confirmed with a clean reproduction: the stream diff closes on en→fr and the Law 'Stored diff' closes on fr→ar. The walker's evidence was confounded, because the tracked-page click they made after opening the diff already collapses it on its own.
4. **French translates 'lane' as both 'file' and 'voie'.** Confirmed on the Storage header and hover, the export hover, the Collection summary, the retired notice, and the consent hint in protected mode. In fr.json, 26 lane keys use 'file' and 10 use 'voie'; even the proxy and pool hints of the same function disagree.
5. **Chinese lines put an ASCII space after '：' and '。'.** Confirmed in the Storage reading, the Storage disk caveat, the Maps table and the task manager. The existing ooLabelText/ooLabelHtml helpers are the fix and are not used at these sites.
6. **New.** Clicking a tracked page on Living sources → Wikipedia reloads the whole panel and collapses an open stream diff (app-map.js:2958).

Scripts, raw JSON and screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/O-recheck/.
